lineage: Provenance: this package FORKS the accepted lead 0a45ddb2 (116.793080), whose own lineage is cbadde77 -> 6ecec8e3 -> cf6d45a8 -> 0a45ddb2; all four are declared as dependencies. Every identity, size, itemisation, bound, cap, price and toy result is restated and re-verified in THIS package; nothing is inherited by citation. This revision (v4) answers the v3 review in full: (1) the walk schedule is now explicit and closed - per chain the generating node builds and RETAINS the value-indexed gap table [g]Q (the affine point for every even g < 2^33, 2^32 entries at 96 bytes) by a unit walk T_{j+1} = T_j + [2]Q at one batched addition per entry (charged as the gap-tables term, 2^65 chains x 2^32 entries), every one of the L steps then READS its addend from the table by gap value (the read is in the 47-instruction walk overhead), rare gaps above 2^33 split into two entries against the split-gaps reserve, and the 2^16 lockstep segments share the retained table with one Montgomery inversion per round - so the addend points are available at every step with no recomputation, the build charged once in work and once in the generating-node memory (the v3 text wrongly said the points were never stored, which the toy contradicted); (2) C5 is re-derived with two failure channels - the off-diagonal Poisson(0.51) tail at the 2^20 cap is (e mu/t)^t = exp(-1.42e7), and the diagonal challenges (z = a/a' for a baby base a over a giant base a', over the six twists) make all L shared-w positions true matches and abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 over all base pairs, the same single event that would break C4 and C7 - both channels are far below 2^-40 and charged inside the common cap deduction; (3) N is the smallest exact multiple of 2^64 with 6N^2/m >= 0.51, so 2^64 x L = N is an integer identity and every chain has exactly L = 3534305155321689 steps (the v3 N was not a multiple of 2^64). The standing fork changes against the lead remain: K = 51/100 (jungjipdo's own margin; the lead took 52/100) and the per-record charge 160 over the 33-line six-limb itemisation (walk 33, three relay hops at 26, owner 17 baby / 11 giant; maximal listing 128/122 - a 25 percent margin, the same discipline as the lead's 26 percent over 143, where the lead charged 180), with every shared price re-derived in proof.md section 3. Net: W = 141260229321733040345609882975462768 units, score 116.765839, a gain of 0.027241 bits on the accepted lead - about 0.008 from K, about 0.013 from the charge, with the honest repricing of the shared terms costing 0.0067 back against our own earlier revisions.
work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = records + per-node fixed work + comparisons + gap tables + candidate re-walk + strand starts + segment starts + status tree + base H-primes + walk list + split gaps + candidate multiplications + kept blocks + candidate copy + Lemma 1, with records = 2N x 2000 x (1 + 160/2000), N = 65196422678611482903494932429799424 = 2^64 x L per side (L = 3534305155321689 steps per chain, all w distinct), m = (r-1)/2^20, K = 51/100; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. W(2^20) = 141260229321733040345609882975462768 units exactly. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.765839 = 116765839/1000000.
heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is at least 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39950 at the lower bound K = 0.51 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.51 x (1 + 2^-54.2)). Support: Lemma 4 (the six-fold symmetry and the parity key make the six orbit images of one record share one key and one comparison), the L-entry walk list giving exactly N = 2^64 x L distinct scalars per side, the diagonal collapse K' = K(1 - (L-1)/L^2), the three coverage toys (d = 32/64/128 at r ~ 2^27.6/2^29.7/2^31.7, measured 0.4167/0.4333/0.3333 against predicted 0.3974/0.3913/0.3974, z = +0.43/+0.94/-1.43) and the end-to-end toy (measured 0.3833 against 0.3935 predicted, z = -0.23).

H2 and H2' (supply only): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6503) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list (a gap above 2^33 splits into two table entries against the reserve). Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

Caps C1-C8 (ours, every tail rounded towards the larger probability): C1 comparisons per node (Bernstein, 2^-94845 over all nodes); C2 head-slot depth (Poisson 0.392, tail 2^-82.6 over 2^117 slots); C3 node record-count deviations (Chernoff 2^-3008); C4 false candidate pairs - a compared pair already agrees on the 84 routing and 33 slot key bits, so false matches cost 2^-75 per comparison, expected N^2/2^192 = 2^39.30, cap 2^44 with Chernoff tail (e mu/t)^t = 2^-5.7e13; C5 true matches, two channels - off-diagonal Poisson(0.51) tail exp(-1.42e7) = 2^-2.0e7 at the 2^20 cap, and the diagonal challenges z = a/a' which abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 (the same single event that would break C4 and C7); C6 candidate sinks (owner lists: per-node mean 2^-44.7 against 2^16 slots, tail 2^-3.9e6; generating-node kept blocks: mean 2^20.30 against 2^24 slots, tail 2^-3.8e7); C7 re-walk key repeats (4-step kept cap, 1.7e-194 over all chains); C8 node overflow against the pool capacity ceil(2^33.32) records (Chernoff 2^-1309819329 plus a 2^-20 modelling budget). Success claimed = 0.39950 - 2^-40 (every cap tail, including both C5 channels) - 2^-20 (C8 modelling) = 0.395 >= 0.39.
limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.
H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence).

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; the cluster model (no remote-memory instruction, 512-byte block transfers charged to sender and receiver, waiting nodes free) is the accepted lineage's definition restated here, and every shared price is re-derived in proof.md section 3 rather than inherited.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.490 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.5.

The per-record charge 160 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 128/122; it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0272 bits under the accepted lead; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K 0.51, charge 180->160 at matched 25/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds; a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
